# Session preparation

## Installing R packages

You will need to install the following packages from CRAN:
```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(c("patchwork", "dplyr", "tidyr", "suncalc", "remotes",
  "tidyverse", "classInt"))
```
<br>
And from GitHub:

- **FathomR**
```{r, eval = FALSE}

remotes::install_github("Fish-Tracking-Data-Team/FathomR",
  build_vignettes = TRUE,
  dependencies = TRUE)

```

- **RangeR**
```{r, eval = FALSE}

remotes::install_github("Fish-Tracking-Data-Team/RangeR", 
                        build_vignettes = TRUE,
                        dependencies = TRUE)
```

- **gapFinder**
```{r, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("IMOS-AnimalTracking/gapFinder",
  build_opts = c("--no-resave-data", "--no-manual"),
  build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

- **remora**

```{r, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("IMOS-AnimalTracking/remora",
  build_vignettes = TRUE,
  dependencies = TRUE)
```

For interactive use, set your working directory to the folder containing the workshop materials. When rendering, R Markdown uses the directory containing this document:

```{r}
options(width = 70) # Console width setting
```

<br>

# Analysis Session 1

## 1.1 FathomR - Rapid Ingestion of Fathom csv files into R

### 1.1.1 Load the FathomR package
```{r FathomR-package}

library(FathomR)
library(dplyr)

```

### 1.1.2 Inspect logfile metadata and schema

```{r FathomR-logfiles}

# inspect logfile metadata  
log.file.details <- inspect_receiver_log_index(
  directory_path = './Data/FathomR/'
)

fathom.schema <- peek_fathom_schema(
  directory_path = './Data/FathomR/'
)

```

### 1.1.3 Ingest logfiles 

```{r FathomR-ingest}

# ingest fathom logfiles into a list object
data <- parse_fathom_files(
  './Data/FathomR/', output = 'list'
)


# alternatively, ingest fathom logfiles into individual tibbles
parse_fathom_files(
        './Data/FathomR/', output = 'env',
        as_tibble = TRUE
)

```

### 1.1.4 Leveraging FathomR data structure

```{r FathomR-datastructures}

# Removing receiver self-transmitter detections

self.transmit.ids <- cfg_transmitter$`Full ID`

# isolate animal detections

animal.dets <- det %>%
    filter(!`Full ID` %in% self.transmit.ids)

```


## 1.2. Range Testing - Drift Range Test (RangeR package and DriftR app demo)

### 1.2.1 Load required packages
```{r ranger-packages}

library(FathomR)
library(RangeR)

```

### 1.2.2 Load Receiver Logfiles

Parse the receiver logfiles into a list object containing the detections and diagnostics needed for the workflow.

```{r drift-logfiles}

data <- FathomR::parse_fathom_files(
  "./Data/range_test/drift_test/logfiles",
  output = "list"
)

```

### 1.2.3 Define Transmission Source

Set the transmission source for the workflow.

```{r drift-trans-source}
transmission_source <- "VR100"
```

### 1.2.4 Define Station Metadata

Station metadata can be created in place or read from a file. resolve_station_location() standardises the input and returns the selected station row together with a station_location vector that can be passed into downstream RangeR functions. 

```{r drift-station-metadata}
stations <- data.frame(
  latitude = c(-42.6665),
  longitude = c(147.9767),
  Serial = c(548851)
)

stations <- resolve_station_location(
  stations = stations,
  station_row = NULL
)

```

If you have multiple stations, either set station_row explicitly or leave it as NULL in an interactive session to choose a row.

### 1.2.5 Select Transmitters and Devices

``` {r drift-devices}

det <- data$det # create a data from of detections 

transmitters <- select_range_transmitter(
  det = det,
  transmission_source = transmission_source
)

devices <- select_devices(
  det = det,
  transmission_source = transmission_source
)

```

### 1.2.6 Qualify Receiver Receiver Diagnostics 

``` {r drift-diagnostics}

diag <- data$diag

deployment_times <- get_deployment_time(
  diag_fast = diag,
  min_tilt = 0,
  max_tilt = 60,
  n = 5
)

plot_deployment_windows(
  diag_data = diag,
  deployment_time_result = deployment_times
)

# Optional: manual modification of deployment times
# deployment_times$maxTime <- deployment_times$maxTime + 86400

```

### 1.2.7 Run Drift Range Analysis 

``` {r drift-analysis}

range_est <- run_drift_range_analysis(
  det = det,
  start_time = deployment_times$minTime,
  end_time = deployment_times$maxTime,
  devices = devices,
  transmitter_ids = transmitters,
  station_location = stations$station_location,
  transmission_source = transmission_source,
  synthetic_transmit_data = NULL,
  time_buffer = 5,
  dist_threshold = 1200,
  prediction_distance_max = 800
)

```

### 1.2.8 Plot Results  

``` {r drift-plots}

plot_drift_results(
  range_est,
  title = if (length(transmitters) == 1) {
    paste0("Detection curve for ", transmitters)
  } else {
    "Detection curves"
  },
  subtitle = paste("Transmitters:", paste(transmitters, collapse = ", ")),
  x_limits = c(0, 1200),
  x_breaks = seq(0, 1200, 100)
)

```

## 1.3 Static Range Test

### 1.3.1 Load required packages
```{r static-packages}

library(FathomR)
library(RangeR)
library(padr)
library(data.table)
library(tibble)
library(gridExtra)

```

### 1.3.2 Identify stations

``` {r static-stations}
# load station metdata
stations <- readr::read_csv('./Data/range_test/static_test/metadata/deployment_metadata.csv')

# standardise stations dataframe
receiver_prep <- RangeR::prepare_distance_df(stations, lat_col = 'latitude',
                                            long_col = 'longitude', station_col = 'Station', 
                                            serial_col = 'Serial')

                                  
# Load receiver logfiles 
data <- parse_fathom_files('./Data/range_test/static_test/logfiles') # parse fathom interleaved csv

```

### 1.3.3 Calculate distances between stations

``` {r static-distances}

# calculate distances between the reference and all other stations
distance_df <- RangeR::receiver_separations(receiver_prep, reference_station = c('RT2'))

```

### 1.3.4 Identify Deployment Times

```{r static-deployment}

# computet the deployment times using receiver diagnostics 
deployment_times <- get_deployment_time(data$diag, min_tilt = 6, max_tilt = 40, 5)


# check deployment duration 
as.numeric(deployment_times$maxTime - deployment_times$minTime)

# plot receiver diagnostics (tilt and noise)
plot_deployment_windows(data$diag, deployment_times, diagnostic = 'both')

```

### 1.3.5 Extract range transmitter ID

``` {r static-transmitter}

# extract the transmitter programming of the reference station
transmitters <- transmitter_config(data$cfg_transmitter, distance_df)

```


### 1.3.6 Calculate receiver detection range

``` {r static-range}

range <- calculate_range(data$det, transmitters,
                        distance_df, 
                        deployment_times$minTime,
                        deployment_times$maxTime, 
                        nom_delay = transmitters$nom_delay,
                        prediction_distance_max = 1500)

```

## 1.4. Receiver performance and diagnostics - gapFinder package walkthrough

### Load packages

```{r gapfinder-packages}
library(FathomR)
library(gapFinder)
library(patchwork)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(suncalc)
```

### Load receiver logs

Load Fathom csv files exported from [Fathom Central](https://fathomcentral.com/learn) and stored on disk:

```{r gapfinder-load}
fathom_dets <- parse_fathom_files("Data/gapFinder/Fathom",
  output = "list")
```

### Match deployment metadata

The raw receiver log files will need to be matched to receiver deployment metadata, so that gapFinder can assing them to the correct stations, and process only the data for when the receivers were in the water. 

```{r gapfinder-metadata}
# Example metadata file
meta_file <- read.csv("Data/gapFinder/Receiver metadata.csv")

meta_file

```
```{r, results = "hide"}
# Match metadata and Fathom files
dets_sort <- match_meta(input = fathom_dets,
  path_meta = "Data/gapFinder/Receiver metadata.csv",
  receiver_id = "receiver_name",
  transmitter_id = "transmit_id",
  type = "type",
  station_name = "station_name",
  deploy_datetime = "receiver_deployment_datetime",
  recover_datetime = "receiver_recovery_datetime",
  lat = "receiver_deployment_latitude",
  lon = "receiver_deployment_longitude",
  tz = "UTC")
```
```{r, gapFinder-match_meta}
names(dets_sort)

# Detections
head(as.data.frame(dets_sort$det))

# Diagnostic
head(as.data.frame(dets_sort$diag))
```

### Daily transmissions and detections

The first step in data analyses is to indentify how many range test transmissions could be successfuly detected (detection efficiency). This step can be done at both **daily** resolution, or separately for day/night periods (using ```circadian = TRUE```). There is no need to set timezones, gapFinder will automatically use your receiver deployment locations to figure it out.

```{r gapfinder-daily-dets}
# Calculate daily detections
daily_dets <- get_daily_dets(input = dets_sort,
  circadian = TRUE,
  path_meta = "Data/gapFinder/Receiver metadata.csv",
  receiver_id = "receiver_name",
  transmitter_id = "transmit_id",
  station_name = "station_name",
  type = "type",
  deploy_datetime = "receiver_deployment_datetime",
  recover_datetime = "receiver_recovery_datetime",
  lat = "receiver_deployment_latitude",
  lon = "receiver_deployment_longitude",
  tz = "UTC")

head(daily_dets)
```

#### Calculating daily detection ranges

The next step will be to calculate the daily ranges for each station in the array. If you run ```get_daily_dets``` with ```circadian = TRUE```, the ranges will be automatically calculated separately for day/night periods. Otherwise, ranges will be calculated with daily resolution.

The machine learning correction model will also be applied to all calculated ranges, if receiver diagnostic data is available (receiver was recovered). 

```{r gapfinder-daily-ranges}
daily_ranges <- get_daily_ranges(input = daily_dets,
  diag_data = dets_sort,
  parallel = TRUE)

names(daily_ranges)
daily_ranges$global # Global parameters
head(daily_ranges$ranges)
head(daily_ranges$curves)
```

We can use the $ranges and $curves objects to reconstruct the daily range curves for each day (and circadian period) of data available.

```{r gapfinder-curves, fig.height = 12}
dates <- seq(as.Date("2022-12-29", tz = "UTC"),
  as.Date("2023-01-02", tz = "UTC"),
  1)

dates

for (i in 1:length(dates)) {
  aux_plot <- ggplot() + theme_bw() +
    geom_line(data = subset(daily_ranges$curves,
        station_name == "MIL 10" &
        date == dates[i]),
      aes(x = x, y = p),
      linewidth = 1,
      colour = "dodgerblue") +
    geom_point(data = subset(daily_ranges$ranges,
        station_name == "MIL 10" &
        date == dates[i]),
      aes(x = max_distance_detected, y = daily_efficiency),
      size = 3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, lty = "dashed") +
    labs(x = "Distance (m)", y = "Detection prob (%)",
      title = paste("Date:", dates[i])) +
    facet_wrap(~circadian)

  # Combine plots
  if (i == 1) {
    plot_curve <- aux_plot
  } else {
    plot_curve <- plot_curve / aux_plot
  }
}

plot_curve
```

gapFinder also has a **range diagnostics** function, that returns several summary statistics of range for each station (and circadian period).

```{r gapfinder-diagnostics}
diag_ranges <- range_diag(input = daily_ranges,
  station_order = c("MIL 10"))

as.data.frame(diag_ranges)
```

We can use $ranges to plot the range timeseries (range = modelled range; cor_range = machine learning corrected ranges) for each station.

```{r gapfinder-ranges-plot}
ranges_long <- daily_ranges$ranges %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(cor_range, range),
    names_to = "range_type",
    values_to = "range_value"
  )

plot_ranges1 <- ggplot(ranges_long) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line(aes(x = date, y = range_value, colour = range_type)) +
  facet_wrap(~circadian, nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Range (m)", colour = "",
    title = "MIL 10 daily ranges")

plot_ranges2 <- ggplot(ranges_long) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x = circadian,
    y = range_value,
    group = interaction(circadian, range_type),
    colour = range_type)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Range (m)", colour = "")

plot_ranges <- (plot_ranges1 | plot_ranges2) + plot_layout(guides = "collect")

plot_ranges
```

#### Environmental drivers of detection range

First we need to add circadian periods to the diagnostic data (OBS: to be added as a function in the package in the next update).

gapFinder defines day/night periods using **nautical dawn** and **nautical dusk** as the periods of reference. 

First, lets use a single location reference point:

```{r gapfinder-circadian}

lat <- dets_sort$diag$receiver_deployment_latitude[1]

lat 

lon <- dets_sort$diag$receiver_deployment_longitude[1]

lon 

# Parse timestamps in UTC, then derive the local time and local date
dets_sort$diag <- dets_sort$diag %>%
  mutate(
    local_time = with_tz(Time, "Australia/Hobart"),
    date = as.Date(local_time) # local calendar date, used for the join
  )

# Sunrise and sunset for each local date at receiver deployment
sun <- getSunlightTimes(
  date = unique(dets_sort$diag$date),
  lat = lat,
  lon = lon,
  keep = c("nauticalDawn", "nauticalDusk"),
  tz = "Australia/Hobart"
)

head(sun)

# Assign day/night categories
dets_sort$diag <- dets_sort$diag %>%
  left_join(
    sun %>% dplyr::select(date, nauticalDawn, nauticalDusk),
    by = "date"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    circadian = case_when(
      local_time >= nauticalDawn & local_time < nauticalDusk ~ "day",
      TRUE ~ "night"
    )
  )

# Sanity check
table(dets_sort$diag$circadian, useNA = "ifany")
```

Plot diagnostic data and daily ranges:

```{r gapfinder-diag-plots, fig.height = 10, fig.width = 10}
plot_eff <- ggplot() + theme_bw() + 
  geom_line(data = daily_ranges$ranges,
    aes(x = date, y = daily_efficiency)) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Efficiency (%)") +
  facet_wrap(~circadian, nrow = 2)

plot_temp <- ggplot() + theme_bw() +
  geom_line(data = dets_sort$diag,
    aes(x = Time, y = as.numeric(`Ambient Temperature (deg C)`))) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Temperature (°C)") +
  facet_wrap(~circadian, nrow = 2)

plot_noise <- ggplot() + theme_bw() +
  geom_line(data = dets_sort$diag,
    aes(x = Time, y = as.numeric(`Noise Mean (mV)`))) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Noise (mV)") +
  facet_wrap(~circadian, nrow = 2)

plot_diag <- plot_eff | plot_temp | plot_noise
```

```{r gapfinder-combined, fig.height = 10, fig.width = 12}
plot_ranges / plot_diag
```
